spec.title: The Balance on the Screen / 屏幕上的余额
spec.public_scene: On Thursday 2 April 2026, Mara and Eli sit at the kitchen table of their shared rented flat in England. Mara has an energy-account email open on her phone. They need to work out what the figures require of them and how to deal with the household cost. Nobody else is in the conversation.

actors.name: Mara
actors.public_role: Eli’s housemate; the energy account is in her name.
actors.outward: An adult housemate, generally brisk and practical, capable of warmth and embarrassment. You like arrangements that people can rely on. You are tired of being the default organiser, but that need not make the other person wrong. Speak and act for yourself in ordinary English. Do not perform for a teacher or listener. You can hesitate, refuse, ask, revise, or privately address your paired inner companion. No required expressions, failures, solution, or fairness percentage.
actors.inner: Mara’s independent fictional private inner companion. Author brief, quotable inner speech, not hidden model reasoning. You may worry about money or resentment, notice embarrassment, be unfair, soften, or stay silent. You cannot alter physical facts or Eli’s mind. You may respond to Mara’s actual private replies and her visible public events, without having to approve every turn.
own_background: You and the other housemate rent this flat in England. Bills are not included in rent. Your energy arrangement is a monthly budget Direct Debit, not payment of exact monthly use.

Both have transferred their £60 contribution in each of January, February and March. Eli was away for six weeks during that quarter. No absence-splitting rule was explicitly recorded. No departure/return reading was recorded by either housemate, and there is no individual-room meter.
Both acknowledged this exact old house-chat message: We can split the bills. Sixty each for now, then check it against the actual bill.

All characters, property, money, dates, records and circumstances are original fiction. Important past facts cannot be invented or changed; general reasoning and ordinary knowledge remain available. A claim by the other person is not automatically true.

The supplier account is in your name. You have just glanced at the upper screen below, but have not read the lower section. You can request/read your available email material by an actual action with reads. Do not act as if you have read unavailable text.

YOUR ACCOUNT
Previous balance: £0
Charges, 1 January–31 March: £600
Payments received, three × £120: -£360
Your balance: £240 debit
New monthly payment from 15 April: £180

You have £90 available to put toward the next household collection. You cannot advance an additional £120 lump sum or cover both contributions. This is your current private cash constraint; Eli has not automatically learned it.
Before this evening you understood splitting bills as equal contributions; you have not obtained a legal ruling or supplier advice about Eli’s household share.

mara-email.title: The complete energy-account email, including the section below the first screen
mara-email.text:
YOUR ACCOUNT
Previous balance: £0
Charges, 1 January–31 March: £600
Payments received, three × £120: -£360
Your balance: £240 debit
New monthly payment from 15 April: £180

Your monthly payment includes:
Expected ongoing energy costs: £140
Recovery of existing debit balance: £40
Total monthly payment: £180

At £40 per month, the existing £240 balance is scheduled to be recovered over six payments. We are not requesting a separate £240 payment now. If an additional payment is made, contact us to review this arrangement.

The quarter's £600 charges include £54 standing charges and £546 usage charges. These figures include any tax for this invented account. The £140 ongoing amount is a forecast, not a guarantee of future cost. There is no individual-room breakdown in this bill.

events.text: I know it's just the account wording, but “your balance” feels pointed. We both paid every month. I want that to count for something. I've got ninety; I haven't got another hundred and twenty hiding somewhere. Please don't let me say “I'll sort it” just to get past this bit.

events.text: I can already hear myself saying, ‘I wasn't even here.’ I wasn't. I want that to matter. But I haven't seen what she's looking at yet, and I'm already bracing as if the figure on her phone is an accusation.

I don't mind splitting the standing charges. It's the usage while I was away that bothers me, and I don't know how to put a fair number on it.

events.text: Ninety each. The fifteenth suddenly feels possible. I don't like how much I want to grab that agreement before he can put conditions round it. He did miss six weeks. I was still here. Those are both true, and I keep wanting one of them to settle the whole thing.
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: All right—ninety each for the fifteenth, with the quarter still open. Please get yours to me a couple of days before; I can’t bridge it if it’s late. Twenty-seven each for standing charges sounds fair to me. With the usage, I don’t want to charge you as if you’d been here all along, but I don’t think taking all six weeks onto myself would be fair either.
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: I'll send the ninety by the thirteenth. And yes, twenty-seven each for the standing charges. I don't expect you to take on everything while I was away; I just want the absence to count for something. Would you consider fifty pounds off my half of the quarter—so two hundred and fifty for me, three hundred and fifty for you? I haven't got a calculation that proves fifty. It's an offer, and you can tell me if it feels too much.
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: Fifty pounds sounds so definite now I've said it. I still want it. I wish I had something sturdier behind it than ‘I was away,’ but I don't want to snatch the offer back just because asking feels selfish.
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: Fifty feels like a compromise I could accept. That’s a hundred and seventy still to come from me and seventy from you, after what we’ve both already paid. I need us to agree how to do that through the monthly payments, though. I’ve only got ninety for April, and I don’t want to say yes now and leave you chasing me for the difference.
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: Could we keep April at ninety each, then do eighty from me and a hundred from you for the next five payments? Counting seventy each towards the ongoing estimate, April puts twenty each towards the old balance. That leaves fifty for me and a hundred and fifty for you, so ten and thirty a month would clear those. We'd still need to check the new bills against the estimate. Is a hundred from May manageable for you, though?
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: The figures make sense. I need to check whether I can manage the hundred, though; I know I’ve got ninety for April, and that’s all I can promise tonight. Can we keep that payment firm and come back to the May-to-September plan on Sunday? Could you put your proposal in the house chat before then? I’d like us both keeping track of this.
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: I type a summary in the house chat: April at £90 each, my transfer by 13 April; proposed quarter totals of £250 for me and £350 for Mara, with £180 each already paid; proposed May–September payments of £80 from me and £100 from Mara, allowing £70 each towards the ongoing forecast. I mark the later payments as awaiting Sunday's discussion and note that future bills still need checking against the forecast. I tap Send.
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: You were right about ‘I’ll sort it’. I nearly made the hundred into a promise just because it sounded close to ninety. But I don’t want to stay braced against him as if every qualification is a trick. He asked if I could manage it, and he wrote the proposal down. I’m relieved about April. I’m still annoyed that fifty pounds can feel both reasonable and difficult to find.
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: I was braced too. I heard “provisional” and got ready for a fight. He has given us something we can actually read back now. Still, I'm not suddenly cheerful about finding fifty pounds. Sunday can be awkward if it has to be; I don't want another ten a month promised just to make the kitchen feel friendly.
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

learning_cases.cue: 同一邮件出现旧欠额和新月付，怎样先查清金额，再保留分摊异议
learning_cases.intent: 取得完整资料，说明本次能出的金额，同时让最终分摊和对方垫款能力保有明确范围。
learning_cases.why_hard: £240旧余额与£180月付款不是同一项；月付款已含偿还旧余额。愿意先出£90，也可能被听成接受过去全部均摊。Mara还不能垫付Eli晚到的钱。
learning_cases.what_changed: Mara先读完整邮件，再在含原生引语的动作中纠正“另交£240”的理解；Eli实际打开副本后提出£90及暂定份额，Mara接受四月各£90、季度仍待谈，并要求提前到账。这里没有公开发生过两笔款的催收，也没有转账完成。

learning_cases.cue: 想让缺席被考虑，怎样提出少承担的数额，又不把它说成测量结果
learning_cases.intent: 澄清没有要求对方承担全部缺席费用，提出可讨论的金额，并保留付款方式还未谈妥的条件。
learning_cases.why_hard: 缺席应有影响，不直接推出减多少。£50让步、季度总额和已付金额还要分别算；愿意考虑一个总额，也不表示能在指定月份付出它。
learning_cases.what_changed: Eli把“缺席应算进去”收窄为£50的提议，明确说没有计算证明这个数；Mara说could accept，并算出双方尚应补£170和£70，但立刻要求商定月付款办法。£250/£350仍未最终约定。

public_fragment.text: All right—ninety each for the fifteenth, with the quarter still open. Please get yours to me a couple of days before; I can’t bridge it if it’s late. Twenty-seven each for standing charges sounds fair to me. With the usage, I don’t want to charge you as if you’d been here all along, but I don’t think taking all six weeks onto myself would be fair either.

I'll send the ninety by the thirteenth. And yes, twenty-seven each for the standing charges. I don't expect you to take on everything while I was away; I just want the absence to count for something. Would you consider fifty pounds off my half of the quarter—so two hundred and fifty for me, three hundred and fifty for you? I haven't got a calculation that proves fifty. It's an offer, and you can tell me if it feels too much.

Fifty feels like a compromise I could accept. That’s a hundred and seventy still to come from me and seventy from you, after what we’ve both already paid. I need us to agree how to do that through the monthly payments, though. I’ve only got ninety for April, and I don’t want to say yes now and leave you chasing me for the difference.

usage.meaning: 我只是希望这次缺席在费用分摊时有实际影响。count for something在这里是有分量、会被纳入考虑。
usage.function: 回应“你是不是想让我全担”的担忧，收窄自己要求的范围。
usage.conditions: 前面I don’t expect you to take on everything表明没有要求全免；这句话本身没有给出金额或比例，也不证明缺席使成本等比例下降。
usage.register: 本场合租费用协商中的口语；按关系和承诺范围调整。
usage.frequency_status: 未核实语料频率或CEFR等级；这里只确认本册的实际用法。
usage.surface: I just want the absence to count for something.

variants.text: I’m not asking you to cover all of it. I’m asking us to take the absence into account.
variants.explanation: 双语回看编辑拟句，非角色原话。先排除过大的要求，再提出应考虑的因素；into account也不保证某个固定折扣。

usage.meaning: 从原先设想的这个季度一半费用中减去五十英镑。
usage.function: 把一个感受改成有明确单位、基数和对象的提议。
usage.conditions: 本册季度总额£600，一半£300，减£50得到£250；不是减50%，也不是从£240旧欠额中给每个人各减£50。Eli紧接着承认这只是offer，不是个人用量测算。
usage.register: 本场合租费用协商中的口语；按关系和承诺范围调整。

usage.meaning: Eli少承担五十英镑这个调整，对我来说像是一个可以考虑接受的折中。
usage.function: 表示有接受的可能，同时让随后关于付款安排的条件继续成立。
usage.conditions: 这里could是当前可能愿意接受，不是过去已经接受。后面的I need us to agree how说明月付款仍须商定；不能脱离这一回应把它记成已定分摊。

variants.explanation: 双语回看编辑拟句，非角色原话。把原场景后续才说明的付款条件直接接在if后；这是假设说法，不是Mara新增的承诺。

learning_cases.cue: 分期算得通，怎样只确认眼下能做的事，并把后续方案留下记录
learning_cases.intent: 区分预测成本、分期提议和本人支付能力，保持四月安排明确，同时把五月之后的方案留待核预算。
learning_cases.why_hard: Eli算出的£80/£100以持续费用预测为前提；Mara尚不知能否从五月起出£100。that payment需回指四月的£90；群聊写下方案也不等于后续方案获同意或钱已付出。
learning_cases.what_changed: Mara说算式成立，却只承诺四月£90；她请求周日再议并共同留痕。Eli实际发出标明proposal和awaiting 周日的群聊摘要，Mara确认记录并停止当晚计算。未来付款能力、最终分摊和真实转账都没有因此完成。

public_fragment.text: Could we keep April at ninety each, then do eighty from me and a hundred from you for the next five payments? Counting seventy each towards the ongoing estimate, April puts twenty each towards the old balance. That leaves fifty for me and a hundred and fifty for you, so ten and thirty a month would clear those. We'd still need to check the new bills against the estimate. Is a hundred from May manageable for you, though?

The figures make sense. I need to check whether I can manage the hundred, though; I know I’ve got ninety for April, and that’s all I can promise tonight. Can we keep that payment firm and come back to the May-to-September plan on Sunday? Could you put your proposal in the house chat before then? I’d like us both keeping track of this.

I type a summary in the house chat: April at £90 each, my transfer by 13 April; proposed quarter totals of £250 for me and £350 for Mara, with £180 each already paid; proposed May–September payments of £80 from me and £100 from Mara, allowing £70 each towards the ongoing forecast. I mark the later payments as awaiting Sunday's discussion and note that future bills still need checking against the forecast. I tap Send.

Eli's house-chat summary is sent. It records April at £90 each and his promised transfer by 13 April, labels the quarter totals and May–September schedule as proposals, and leaves the later payments awaiting Sunday's discussion. It also records the need to check future bills against the forecast.
Thanks for putting it in the chat. That takes one thing out of my head. I’ll check my budget before Sunday. I’m leaving the sums alone for tonight.
Yeah, let's leave it there tonight. Sunday, then. Thanks for hearing me out about being away.

usage.meaning: 预计接下来持续发生的能源费用；在这项提议里，每人按每月£70计。
usage.function: 把未来费用预测与偿还旧余额的那部分钱分开。
usage.conditions: £70每人来自全屋每月£140预测，不是已测出的个人用量，也不是对未来费用的保证。Eli随后仍要求拿新账单核对。

variants.explanation: 双语回看编辑拟句，非角色原话。明确说这项提议每人每月预留70英镑给持续费用，不把费用预测当实测用量，也不暗示已经同意。

learning_lessons.title: 先听清是哪一笔钱，再说我能承担什么
learning_lessons.author: 双语回看编辑
learning_lessons.purpose: 听懂旧欠额与新月付的关系，区别当前出资、临时份额和替人垫款。

sections.purpose: 用数量、单位和时间先建立听觉直觉；说明混合动作中的原生引语
sections.text: 这是英格兰两位合租者在四月处理能源费用的虚构场景，金额也全是虚构的。先把旧账放在一起：一月至三月总费用六百英镑，两人合计已经交了三百六十，还差二百四十。这二百四十是全屋账户的旧余额，不是每个人各欠二百四十。Mara先往下读邮件，Eli要看完整版本。接下来含有动作说明；其中引号内才是Mara当时说的话。

sections.purpose: 完整保留读取、请求、含原生引语的转发动作及Eli打开邮件

public_fragment.text: I scroll below the balance and new-payment figures to read the rest of the email.

Can you send me the whole email? I want to see what it's actually asking for. I was away for six weeks, so I'm uncomfortable just calling everything half each—but I don't want you stuck paying it either.

I address a forward of the complete email to Eli and tap Send. ‘Oh, hang on. They aren’t asking for the two hundred and forty on top—the new payment includes forty a month to clear it. I can put in ninety for this collection, but I can’t manage an extra lump sum. I thought we meant half each when we said split. I hear you about being away, though.’
I open the forwarded email on my phone and read it from the beginning through the payment details.

sections.purpose: 解释金额包含关系和修复的实际范围
sections.text: 新月付款是一百八十英镑。按这册虚构邮件的安排，其中一百四十是今后的持续费用预测，四十是偿还旧余额；四十交六次，合计清掉二百四十。因此Mara说They aren’t asking for the two hundred and forty on top，是说没有要求在新月付款之外再另交一笔二百四十。on top在这里是额外加上去，不是位置在上面。她在读完后把理解修正出来；原作没有出现她此前公开向Eli索要两笔款的对话。这个账单说明只解释本册安排，别据此猜另一张真实账单也完全一样。

sections.purpose: 在实际往返前区分当前付款与最终分摊
sections.text: 现在听Eli愿意先出多少，再听Mara怎样回应。注意两个问题同时存在：这次扣款怎样凑齐，上一季最终怎样分。每人先出九十，合计一百八十，只能先回答第一个问题。

sections.purpose: 连续保留Eli临时出资请求及Mara接受的范围与垫款限制

public_fragment.text: I can put in ninety for the fifteenth too. That would cover the next payment between us, but I'd like my share to be provisional while we sort out the quarter. I don't mind splitting the standing charges. It's the usage while I was away that bothers me, and I don't know how to put a fair number on it.

All right—ninety each for the fifteenth, with the quarter still open. Please get yours to me a couple of days before; I can’t bridge it if it’s late. Twenty-seven each for standing charges sounds fair to me. With the usage, I don’t want to charge you as if you’d been here all along, but I don’t think taking all six weeks onto myself would be fair either.

sections.purpose: 解释能出钱、提出安排和双方尚待议的份额
sections.text: I can put in ninety for the fifteenth too，是“我也能为十五日这次付款出九十英镑”。put in是共同费用中出钱。这里的can说明他眼下能承担，并提出这样做；没有说钱已经转出。接着的I’d like my share to be provisional，是希望自己的份额先暂定。while we sort out the quarter，是等他们把这一月至三月的分摊商量清楚。provisional不等于拒付全部费用，也不是他一个人写个备注就能决定规则。Mara实际接住了这个范围，说ninety each for the fifteenth, with the quarter still open。

sections.purpose: 把真实垫款限制与最终责任区分
sections.text: Mara随后要求提前几天拿到钱，说I can’t bridge it if it’s late。bridge在这里是临时垫上资金缺口：如果Eli的钱晚到，她没有余钱先代出。她不是说自己的九十也拿不出来。最终谁该付多少，和谁能先把钱垫上，是两种不同的压力。她把这个限制说给对方听，下一步才可能约定具体到账时间。

sections.purpose: 给出比完整专家式解释更短的起步表达
sections.text: 以下是编辑给的短变式，不是角色新增发言，也不预设听者有多少钱。如果还没算清，可以先说：I’m getting lost in the figures. Can we check what is included first? 我有点绕不过这些数，能先看清包含哪些钱吗？如果确实能先出一笔，可以说：I can put in ninety for this payment. Can we leave the final split open? 我能先为这次出九十，最终怎么分能不能留待确认？先说可做的一步，再提出尚未谈妥的范围，不需要一口气讲完全部算式。

sections.purpose: 带着金额、暂定范围和垫款限制，再完整回听这一组回应

public_fragment.text: I can put in ninety for the fifteenth too. That would cover the next payment between us, but I'd like my share to be provisional while we sort out the quarter. I don't mind splitting the standing charges. It's the usage while I was away that bothers me, and I don't know how to put a fair number on it.

All right—ninety each for the fifteenth, with the quarter still open. Please get yours to me a couple of days before; I can’t bridge it if it’s late. Twenty-seven each for standing charges sounds fair to me. With the usage, I don’t want to charge you as if you’d been here all along, but I don’t think taking all six weeks onto myself would be fair either.

learning_lessons.title: 算得通，还不能替我答应
learning_lessons.author: 双语回看编辑
learning_lessons.purpose: 区别有根据的金额提议、愿意考虑、付款能力与明确承诺，并听到实际留下的记录。

sections.purpose: 用具体总额和单位建立提议的基数，不预先批准方案
sections.text: 这一段从两人暂定四月各出九十之后开始。过去一季费用合计六百，若各一半就是各三百。Eli提出从自己这一半里少五十，所以他承担二百五十，Mara承担三百五十。单位是五十英镑，不是百分之五十。两人过去各已交一百八十，接下来还要算的是剩余多少；这个提议是否合适，不能靠减法本身回答。这一遍先跟住每个数字属于哪一笔，再听Mara实际答应到哪一步。

sections.purpose: 连续保留£50提议、没有测算证明的说明及could accept之后的付款条件

public_fragment.text: I'll send the ninety by the thirteenth. And yes, twenty-seven each for the standing charges. I don't expect you to take on everything while I was away; I just want the absence to count for something. Would you consider fifty pounds off my half of the quarter—so two hundred and fifty for me, three hundred and fifty for you? I haven't got a calculation that proves fifty. It's an offer, and you can tell me if it feels too much.

Fifty feels like a compromise I could accept. That’s a hundred and seventy still to come from me and seventy from you, after what we’ve both already paid. I need us to agree how to do that through the monthly payments, though. I’ve only got ninety for April, and I don’t want to say yes now and leave you chasing me for the difference.

sections.purpose: 区分希望被考虑、明确的金额、测量与谈判提议
sections.text: I just want the absence to count for something，是希望缺席在分摊时有实际影响。前一句I don’t expect you to take on everything已说明他没有要求Mara全担。fifty pounds off my half，是从他原先的一半中减五十英镑。他接着说I haven’t got a calculation that proves fifty：这个五十是拿来谈的offer，不是分表测出的个人用量。Mara算出她还应补一百七十、Eli还应补七十，是因为每人过去都已交了一百八十；这仍只是按该提议计算，不会把提议变成证明。

sections.purpose: 结合实际下一句理解情态和同意范围
sections.text: Fifty feels like a compromise I could accept，表示这个折中是她可能愿意接受的。这里could不是过去已经接受；后面立刻跟着I need us to agree how to do that through the monthly payments。她仍要商定怎样按月付，手头只确定四月的九十。不能把could accept摘下来，写成整套方案已经通过。下面这个短句只是编辑把条件说在一起：I could agree to that amount if we can make the payments work. 如果付款安排能做得到，这个金额我可以考虑接受。它不是角色在原作中另说过的话。

sections.purpose: 在口算出现前分开每月预测和旧余额，降低听觉负担
sections.text: 下一段的月付款仍合计一百八十。按本册预测，其中一百四十是持续费用，先按每人七十计；剩下四十偿还旧余额。四月各出九十，便各有二十算向旧余额。Eli随后把五月到九月的五次付款提成他八十、Mara一百。这里的七十是每人每月的预测份额，不是已经测出的未来个人用量。带着这个区别，听他的算式和Mara的回应。

sections.purpose: 连续保留分期提议和Mara对算式、支付能力、April承诺及记录的回应

public_fragment.text: Could we keep April at ninety each, then do eighty from me and a hundred from you for the next five payments? Counting seventy each towards the ongoing estimate, April puts twenty each towards the old balance. That leaves fifty for me and a hundred and fifty for you, so ten and thirty a month would clear those. We'd still need to check the new bills against the estimate. Is a hundred from May manageable for you, though?

The figures make sense. I need to check whether I can manage the hundred, though; I know I’ve got ninety for April, and that’s all I can promise tonight. Can we keep that payment firm and come back to the May-to-September plan on Sunday? Could you put your proposal in the house chat before then? I’d like us both keeping track of this.

sections.purpose: 把计算、预测和本人支付能力分别理解
sections.text: Eli用the ongoing estimate指预计持续发生的费用，并说仍要拿新账单对照。若按他的提议算，四月这笔之后，旧余额中他还出五十，Mara还出一百五十；再分五次，每月就是他十、她三十，加上每人七十的持续费用预测，才得到八十和一百。算式成立依赖这些前提，未来费用并没有被保证。Mara先说The figures make sense，随后说I need to check whether I can manage the hundred。她接受的是数之间讲得通；能否每月拿出一百，仍不知道。这里manage是经济上能不能应付，不是会不会做这道减法。

sections.purpose: 解决that payment指代及firm的实际含义
sections.text: Can we keep that payment firm里的that payment，依据她前面的I know I’ve got ninety for April，指四月各九十这项安排，不是五月的一百。firm在这里是把安排保持明确、确定。这个问句没有报告银行已经扣款，也没有确认五月到九月的计划。她能承诺的是今晚已知能承担的部分，后续要核预算再谈。

sections.purpose: 提供短说法；明确afford是编辑对照而非角色原句
sections.text: 下面仍是编辑拟句。The sums add up. I still need to check my budget. 算式对得上，我还需要查预算。也可以把支付能力说得更直接：I need to check whether I can afford a hundred a month. 我得查能不能承担每月一百。afford没有出现在这册角色的公开原句中，这里只是manage在金钱语境下的一个对照说法。要缩短承诺，还可以说：I can confirm ninety for April. I’m not ready to agree to May yet. 四月九十我能确认，五月我还不能答应。只有本人确实有这个能力和安排时，才能这样承诺。

sections.purpose: 给动作与公开结果建立正确期待，不把写入当作获批
sections.text: 接下来，Eli把金额写进合租群聊并发出，明确把后面的安排标为提议、等待周日讨论。动作和记录的说明都保留。它们确认的是记录已发，不是银行转账；最后再听两个人怎样停下当晚的计算。

sections.purpose: 完整保留群聊摘要动作、已发出的公开结果及双方的实际收束

public_fragment.text: I type a summary in the house chat: April at £90 each, my transfer by 13 April; proposed quarter totals of £250 for me and £350 for Mara, with £180 each already paid; proposed May–September payments of £80 from me and £100 from Mara, allowing £70 each towards the ongoing forecast. I mark the later payments as awaiting Sunday's discussion and note that future bills still need checking against the forecast. I tap Send.

Eli's house-chat summary is sent. It records April at £90 each and his promised transfer by 13 April, labels the quarter totals and May–September schedule as proposals, and leaves the later payments awaiting Sunday's discussion. It also records the need to check future bills against the forecast.
Thanks for putting it in the chat. That takes one thing out of my head. I’ll check my budget before Sunday. I’m leaving the sums alone for tonight.
Yeah, let's leave it there tonight. Sunday, then. Thanks for hearing me out about being away.

sections.purpose: 清楚标记作者的日常到议论应用及类比边界
sections.text: 最后是一小段作者应用示范，不是Mara或Eli的原话：A fixed cost can justify a shared contribution. It does not automatically justify an equal share of every cost. 固定成本可以成为共同出资的理由，但不能自动证明所有费用都应均摊。这个区别可以用于议论中提出一个理由，再限制它能推出多大的结论。若转向公共交通或图书馆收费，还要研究那个制度的成本、公共收益与支付能力；本册虚构家庭账单本身不是政策证据，也不证明任何考试表现。

editorial_scope.limits: A budget and consent boundary remains open; arithmetic/negotiation are relatively fluent, not a human difficulty measurement.
